meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let's discuss it on the way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'судить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we will discuss', paired with 'обсуждать'.

examples.trans: Let's discuss it on the way.

examples.text: Без лишних ушей обсудим твоё назначение.
examples.trans: Without extra ears we will discuss your appointment.
The partners discussed the terms of the deal in detail.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I am her boyfriend, got it?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: Understand, Vitya, the opening is tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крытие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'grand opening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Understand, Vitya, the opening is tomorrow.

examples.text: Я проверяю, всё ли готово к открытию.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.trans: Our hotel must surprise the guests.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дивить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to surprise', paired with 'удивлять'.

examples.trans: Our hotel must surprise the guests.

examples.text: Ты должен очень сильно удивить наших гостей.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke up', paired with 'расставаться'.

examples.text: Нет, я всё решил! Мы с ней точно расстанемся.
examples.trans: No, I have decided everything! She and I will definitely break up.
